title: Video Editor with Motion Graphics |  SaaS Launch Videos + Shorts + YouTube (Long-term, weekly volume)
description:
Hi, I'm Hudson — an Australian founder building software companies. I'm hiring ONE video editor to work with me long-term. Not project-by-project. The same guaranteed volume every single week.



What you'll edit every week:

- 7 short-form videos (Reels/TikTok/Shorts — captions, pacing, hooks, sound design)

- 1 long-form YouTube video (10–15 min — retention editing, b-roll, screen recordings, motion graphics)

- SaaS product launch videos as needed (app demos, animated UI showcases — Apple keynote style, clean and premium)



That's the whole job. One client, predictable volume, paid monthly, every month.



The bar (watch this before applying):





This is the editing standard I'm building toward — motion graphics on nearly every shot, animated text and diagrams, transitions that carry ideas, sound design on every cut. You don't need to be at this level on day one, but you need to already edit in this direction and want to close the gap. If you watched that and thought "I could do most of that," apply. If you thought "that's a whole team," you're probably right that it's not a fit — no hard feelings.



You're a fit if:

- You edit in After Effects (or Blender/Cavalry for graphics), not just Premiere/CapCut — motion design is the core of this job, not a bonus

- You've edited BOTH short-form and long-form before

- You can make software look premium on screen — smooth zooms, animated UI, screen recordings that feel like Apple keynotes

- You design your own sound: swooshes, risers, impacts timed to cuts

- You care about retention and pacing, not just clean cuts



You're NOT a fit if:

- You need briefs explained twice

- You disappear for days without updates

- Your portfolio is wedding videos and vlogs only, or template-pack edits



What you get:

- Guaranteed weekly volume — no chasing clients, no dry months

- Direct line to me (the founder). No account managers. Feedback within hours, not days.

- 13th month pay, paid Philippine holidays after 90 days

- Raises tied to results — if the channel grows, your pay grows



How to apply (read carefully — this is the test):

1. Start your application with the word MANGO so I know you read this far

2. Send exactly 3 links: your best short-form edit, your best long-form edit, and — most important — your best edit showing MOTION GRAPHICS (animated text, diagrams, transitions you designed yourself, not templates)

3. One sentence: pick any 10-second 
nt from The Studio video above and tell me how you'd recreate it (what software, what technique)



Applications that skip any of these steps won't get a reply — not being harsh, it's just the first skill test: following a brief exactly.



Shortlisted editors get a small PAID test project (~$40–50, real footage, ~3 hours of work, 72-hour deadline). I hire from that test, not from interviews.

title: Virtual Operations Assistant, Part-Time
description:
Part-Time Virtual Operations Assistant

The Quiet Bloom Wellness · Remote · Part-Time · Long-Term · $5–$8/hour · 10–12 hrs/week

This is an operations, coordination, and outreach support role for someone who is detail-oriented, proactive, and thrives on keeping a founder focused on decisions, not logistics.

About The Quiet Bloom Wellness

The Quiet Bloom Wellness (TQB) is a luxury, trauma-informed boutique wellness retreat brand for high-achieving women,  with a particular focus on Black women and women of color in executive and C-suite leadership. Founded and led by Marilyn Moore Dyson, Founder & CEO, TQB offers 1:1 Private Bloom Sessions, boutique wellness retreats, and a membership community launching Q3 2026. The Founder's Retreat is planned for Spring 2027 at the Inn at Perry Cabin, Maryland, with a second venue in active discussion at Salamander Resort & Spa, Middleburg, Virginia.

We are a founder-led brand in active launch phase. This role is impactful from day one, and will grow as we grow.

The Primary Goal of This Role

This is an operations role with a revenue mandate. Every system you maintain, every deadline you hold, every outreach
 you draft, and every follow-up you coordinate creates the conditions for TQB revenue to move through four channels:



REVENUE CHANNEL

HOW THIS ROLE ENABLES IT

CAMPAIGN PHASE

Private Bloom Sessions

Keeping the booking system active, confirming sessions, tracking the PBS pipeline, coordinating testimonial collection, and running the first outreach campaign to warm and cold contacts.

Phase 1 — Immediate

Retreat Bookings

Holding retreat logistics and running targeted outreach to fill the Founder's Retreat and Day Retreats — contracts, facilitator agreements, venue timelines, guest communications.

Phase 2 — Month 2–3

Corporate Collaborations

Tracking the corporate outreach pipeline and supporting targeted outreach to organizational partners so no opportunity goes cold between conversations.

Phase 2 — Month 2–3

Membership Launch

Coordinating the Q3 2026 membership launch campaign — tracking configuration milestones, sequencing outreach to warm contacts, and managing the founding member enrollment window.

Phase 3 — Q3 2026



If you do this job well, Marilyn is free to show up for clients, close partnerships, and grow the brand. That is the measure of success in this role.

What You'll Do — Operations & Coordination

Own a master task tracker across all active workstreams — and flag anything at risk of slipping before it does

Send Marilyn a clear weekly summary every Monday: what's done, what's pending, what needs her decision

Coordinate retreat and event logistics — contracts, facilitator agreements, vendor communications, and timelines for the Founder's Retreat and Day Retreats

Maintain a vendor and partner status log and send follow-up correspondence using pre-approved templates in Marilyn's voice

Track corporate partnership pipeline milestones and surface stalled threads before they go cold

Keep the relationship tracker current — advisor calls, partner outreach, membership launch checklist

Monitor grant pipeline deadlines and flag anything coming up within two weeks

Track PBS bookings, client confirmations, and testimonial collection to keep the offer pipeline active

What You'll Do — Outreach & Campaign Support

Outreach is a core part of this role, not a side task. You will build and execute campaigns across all four revenue channels in sequence — starting with Private Bloom Sessions and expanding from there. All outreach drafts are submitted to Marilyn for approval before anything sends. No exceptions.

PHASE

FOCUS

YOUR RESPONSIBILITIES

Phase 1

Immediate

Private Bloom Sessions

Build and maintain a warm and cold contact list for PBS outreach. Draft personalized outreach
s in Marilyn's voice for her approval. Coordinate sends via Flodesk. Track open rates, responses, and booked sessions weekly. Manage follow-up sequences for non-responders. Flag hot leads to Marilyn immediately.

Phase 2

Month 2–3

Corporate & Retreat

Expand outreach to corporate collaboration prospects and Founder's Retreat candidates. Draft targeted outreach and follow-up sequences for Marilyn's approval. Coordinate sends and track pipeline responses. Maintain a live log of outreach status across both channels. Surface stalled conversations and recommend next steps.

Phase 3

Q3 2026

Membership Launch

Coordinate the founding member enrollment campaign in Flodesk. Build the outreach sequence for warm contacts and past PBS clients. Track enrollment numbers against launch targets. Flag open MemberSpace configuration items so the platform is ready before outreach begins.



Across all phases: you draft, coordinate, and track. Marilyn approves all copy and makes all strategic decisions on targeting. Your job is to make sure the pipeline never sits still.

What You Won't Do

Create social media content — we have an Instagram VA for that

Make strategic decisions — your job is to execute, coordinate, and surface; Marilyn leads

Send any outreach or correspondence without Marilyn's explicit approval

Manage our grants consultant or corporate outreach team — you track their milestones, not their work

Handle legal or IP matters

Tools We Use

You don't need to be an expert in all of these — but you need to be comfortable learning quickly and asking when something is unclear.

TOOL

HOW IT'S USED IN THIS ROLE

Google Workspace

Gmail, Drive, Docs, and Sheets are your primary working environment. All tracking, reporting, contact lists, and coordination lives here.

Flodesk

Primary outreach and
 marketing platform. You build and coordinate outreach sequences, confirm delivery, and track campaign performance. Marilyn writes and approves all content before it sends.

Calendly

Client scheduling for Private Bloom Sessions. You monitor bookings and confirm that all confirmation communications go out correctly.

MemberSpace

Membership platform for TQB's Q3 2026 launch. You track configuration milestones and the launch readiness checklist, and flag open items — Marilyn manages the platform directly.

Canva Pro

Access to shared brand assets for coordination purposes only. This is not a design role.

Stripe

Payments. You track PBS session payments in the client log — you do not manage Stripe directly.



Who We're Looking For

2+ years in a virtual operations, project coordination, or OBM role — ideally supporting a founder or small executive team

title: Social Media Content Video Editor
description:
About the role



PEAK Physique Coaching is hiring one high-output, highly reliable Short-Form Video Editor & Content Manager to own our short-form content end to end — from raw footage to published, scroll-stopping Instagram Reels and TikToks, and everything in between.



This is not a "cut the clips and send them back" editing gig. This is a producer-and-manager role. You will edit at a very high level and run the entire posting operation: scheduling, publishing, captions, hashtags, organization, calendar, and reporting. If you only want to edit and hand off, this is not your role.



We move fast, we hold a high bar, and we value people who take real ownership. We care about excellence, integrity, and dependability — do what you say, on time, done right. As the proverb goes, "Do you see a person skilled in their work? They will serve before rulers." We're looking for that person, and we intend to keep them for the long term and pay accordingly.





What you'll actually own



1. High-end short-form editing





Turn raw footage (talking head, gym clips, podcast-style content, B-roll, screenshots) into high-performing 9:16 Reels and TikToks.

Strong hooks, tight pacing, jump cuts, zooms, overlays, sound design, pattern interrupts, and clean, correctly punctuated captions.

Create hook/caption/CTA variations when needed.

Hold brand consistency: pacing, caption style, fonts, colors, visual hierarchy, CTA format.





2. Full posting & channel management





Own the posting calendar and publish on schedule across Instagram and TikTok — you post, not just deliver.

Write and optimize captions, hooks, and hashtags for reach.

Keep the content pipeline full and running without me chasing you.

Basic community management support as needed (organizing comments/DMs into a simple system, flagging leads).





3. Organization & reporting





Keep project folders, versions, exports, and source files clean so nothing is ever lost.

Handle large media transfers reliably (Google Drive, Dropbox, 
, or similar).

Track tasks and deadlines in a simple system (Trello, Notion, ClickUp, or Google Sheets).

Report simple performance numbers (views, saves, shares, comments, leads) and adjust based on what's working.





4. Direct collaboration with me





Meet with me live, every other day (video call). These are working check-ins: review edits, plan the calendar, unblock fast. Reliability here is non-negotiable.

Take direct feedback and implement it immediately, without friction.







Non-negotiable requirements



You must have all of these. If you're missing one, please don't apply.





Fluent English, spoken and written. You must understand nuance, tone, and fitness terminology, and produce captions with zero errors.

Proven short-form editing experience with a portfolio of TikTok/Reels edits you personally made — ideally in fitness, bodybuilding, nutrition, or coaching.

Strong CapCut skills (desktop and/or mobile): templates, subtitles, effects, beat timing, export settings. Canva for covers, callouts, quote cards, and simple graphics.

Availability for a live call every other day and consistent overlap with my working hours (I'm in US Pacific Time). State your available overlap hours in PT.

Reliable high-speed internet for large uploads/downloads, plus a stable, capable editing workstation.

A dependable track record. You hit deadlines, you communicate proactively when something's blocked, and you don't disappear.





Strongly preferred: experience with a creator/brand posting at high volume (multiple videos per day), understanding of direct-response marketing (hooks, pain points, objections, credibility, CTAs), experience repurposing podcast clips into short-form, and familiarity with Premiere, Final Cut, DaVinci Resolve, or After Effects.





? Do NOT apply if...



I'm adding this section specifically because I keep receiving applications from people who aren't a fit. Please respect both our time. Do not apply if:





You have no portfolio, or your portfolio is stock templates, wedding/real-estate/generic edits, or work you didn't personally do. Fitness or creator short-form samples or don't apply.

You are an agency, reseller, or team planning to pass this to someone else. I'm hiring one person I meet with directly. No middlemen.

You can't or won't attend a live call every other day, or you can't overlap with US Pacific Time hours.

You only want to edit and hand off — you're not willing to also manage posting, scheduling, and organization.

Your English isn't strong enough to write flawless captions and understand nuanced feedback.

You need constant supervision, step-by-step hand-holding, or can't make sound creative decisions on your own.

You're juggling many clients and can't commit to fast, consistent turnaround and daily-ish responsiveness.

You send a generic copy-paste application or use AI to write a bot-sounding message with no real substance. I can tell, and it's an instant no.

Your samples show sloppy captions, typos, clipping audio, awkward cuts, or inconsistent formatting. The bar here is high and I don't lower it.







Compensation



[FILL IN: rate/range, e.g. "___–

___/month" or "$___/hour"] — this is a serious, long-term, above-average seat for the right person, with room to grow as the channel scales. I'd rather pay well for one A-player than cheaply for three who need managing.





Deliverables & expectations





Format: 9:16 vertical, platform-native, ready to post (correct resolution, frame rate, safe margins, audio levels, file naming).

Volume: starts at multiple edits per week, ramping to daily as the workflow tightens.

Turnaround: fast and consistent, against an agreed posting calendar.

Quality bar: strong first 2 seconds, clean captions, tight pacing, on-brand look, minimal revisions.





How success is measured: on-time dependable output, edit quality, low revision rate, clear communication, files always in the right place, and improving performance over time (retention, saves, shares, comments, leads).





How to apply — follow this exactly



Applications that skip any step, or ignore the keyword, are deleted unread. This is intentional — it's how I find the people who actually pay attention.





Start your message with the word PEAK-PRODUCER as the first line. (This is how I know you read the whole post.)

Portfolio link: a folder or page of your short-form edits — fitness/creator TikTok & Reels samples first, ideally MP4 files or direct links. No portfolio, no reply.

In 3–5 sentences, describe your editing workflow from raw footage to final export.

Tell me:



Your internet speed (upload and download).

Your editing device specs and which tools you use (CapCut desktop/mobile, Canva, any others).

Your available overlap hours in US Pacific Time, and confirm you can meet live every other day.







In one or two sentences, tell me the single edit or channel you're most proud of and why it performed.





Pre-screen (shortlisted only): you'll edit a 20–40 second sample from raw footage we provide.



I read every application that follows these instructions. Thank you for your time and care — I'm looking forward to finding the right person.

title: Executive Assistant / Project Manager for Busy Medical Expert Witness Consultant
description:
About the Role

I'm a board-certified pediatrician who runs a growing medical expert witness and forensic consulting practice. I need a full-time executive assistant and project manager to run both my legal consulting business and my personal and professional affairs. You will be the operational backbone of everything I do.

This is not an "assign tasks and check in" role — I need someone who can build the operational systems for this business from scratch and then run them independently. You provide the structure and keep me structured — not the other way around. If you've done this before for another business or consultant, I want to hear about it.

Confidentiality is essential. This work involves sensitive legal cases and protected medical information. Discretion and strict confidentiality are non-negotiable requirements of this role.

A Note About Working With Me

I'm a medical expert witness consultant in high demand among attorneys, and I'm also the author of medical review books used by physicians nationwide. My time needs to be spent doing the work — reviewing cases, writing reports, and testifying. I need someone who will keep my work organized and structured, proactively manage deadlines, and make sure nothing falls through the cracks. That means checking in with me regularly, following up without being asked, and keeping things moving. I can't be organizing you — you'll be organizing me.

How We Work Together

I move fast and think out loud. I need someone who can take a rapid stream of ideas, tasks, and priorities — through phone calls, texts,
s, Slack, whatever channel I'm using in the 
nt — and turn them into organized, actionable steps. Sometimes I'll send the same thing twice. Sometimes I'll fire off five
s in a row. Your job is to catch everything, sort through it, ignore the duplicates, and make sure it all gets done. If I throw ten things at you in a five-minute phone call, I expect to see them show up as tasks on a board with deadlines by end of day. Nothing gets lost.

You'll also help me transition to a completely paperless office. That means regular video calls where you can see my workspace, help me prioritize what needs to be scanned and filed, and build a digital organization system so that paper stops piling up. You'll guide the process and I'll do the physical scanning — but you're managing the system.

The Legal Business Has Three Core Areas

1. Inquiry Tracking & Business Development



Monitoring my inbox to ensure every inquiry from attorneys and law firms is caught and responded to promptly

Tracking all inquiries and following up systematically until we're hired or the lead closes

Setting up initial meetings with potential clients

Following up after meetings to keep the process moving



2. Client Onboarding



Once I'm retained, managing the onboarding process — getting a retention agreement in place, setting up the client in FreshBooks, arranging payment details, and creating a Dropbox folder for the case

Making sure every new case is properly set up and ready for my review



3. Active Case Management



Tracking all deadlines and due dates well in advance

Managing my calendar — court dates, depositions, report deadlines

Flagging upcoming reports that are due and keeping me on schedule

Monitoring cases that are waiting on next steps so nothing falls through the cracks

Invoicing and payment tracking through FreshBooks



Personal & Professional Management



Inbox management — triaging my
 daily so I only deal with what needs my attention

Calendar and Calendly management — scheduling, blocking time, coordinating all meetings

Blocking out personal time including vacations every 6 weeks and recurring appointments like weekly massages

Managing personal projects and obligations — tracking action items, deadlines, and follow-ups

Coordinating with and managing multiple contractors and tea
mbers across different projects and time zones

Helping coordinate family health management — scheduling appointments and tracking follow-ups

Overseeing other business projects including a medical publishing company

General organization and follow-through so nothing falls through the cracks



You Are



Highly organized and self-directed — you don't wait to be told what to do next

Fluent in English with excellent written and verbal communication skills

Comfortable communicating by phone with US-based clients including attorneys and law firms in a professional manner

Able to reach me through multiple channels (Slack, text, WhatsApp, phone) and willing to escalate through whatever channel gets my attention when something is time-sensitive — your job is to make sure I see what I need to see, when I need to see it

Experienced in project management and/or executive assistant roles

Experienced building operational systems and workflows from scratch — you've taken a disorganized or early-stage business and created the structure that made it run. This is critical.

Proficient with FreshBooks, Dropbox, Trello, Slack, and Calendly

Prompt and reliable — this business runs on tight timelines and fast turnaround

Comfortable handling confidential and sensitive information with discretion

Comfortable working with a busy professional who needs proactive support, not just task execution



Nice to Have



Familiarity with medical, healthcare, or legal terminology is a plus but not required

Google Drive, MLS / NWMLS, Realist and county record portals, Transaction Desk, Nekst, Follow Up Boss (FUB), Authentisign, and Paperless Pipeline. Familiarity with Dotloop, Skyslope, or DocuSign also helps.

object removal mistakes (trash cans, cords, etc.)

mbers as long-term partners — our current VA has been with us for 5 years. We are looking for someone who wants to grow with us for years, not months.



Who We're Looking For



We hire for character first. Skills can be taught — character cannot. The person we want is:



Proactive — you see a problem coming and act before being told. You don't wait for instructions when the next step is obvious.

Accountable — you own your mistakes, fix them, and never hide bad news. In our business, bad news delivered early saves deals; bad news hidden kills them.

Organized — you manage multiple transactions at once without letting anything slip.

Ethical — you do the right thing when no one is watching.

Committed to personal development — you read, learn, and improve without being pushed.

A team player — you communicate openly and support the people around you.

Helpful -- You have a helpful mindset and are Kind to People.

Communicative -- You know how to communicate by phone and
 and are proactive doing so, not waiting till a problem arrises. 



If that describes you, keep reading. If you're looking for an easy job where you wait to be told what to do, this is not for you.



What You'll Do



Coordinate real estate transactions from signed contract to closing (Transaction Coordination)

Communicate by phone and
 with sellers, buyers, title companies, and utility companies

Read and track title paperwork; follow up with title companies to keep closings on schedule and catch problems early

Prepare and organize closing documents (assignment contracts, addenda, disclosures)

Schedule appointments, walkthroughs, inspections, photos and closings

Create property listings and send them to our cash buyer list 
/SMS blasts)

Call buyers to share available properties and gather feedback

Keep our CRM clean and updated



Requirements



Excellent spoken English with a clear, neutral accent (you will be on the phone with Americans daily)

Excellent written English

At least 1–2 years of VA experience with a US company (real estate experience is a plus, not required — we will train the right person)

Able to work US Eastern Time hours (approx. 9 AM – 6 PM EST)

Reliable computer, backup internet, quiet workspace (no animal noises in the background)

Transaction coordination experience



Pay & Benefits



$5.00–$7.00/hour based on experience

Paid weekly/bi-weekly, on time, every time

13th Month Pay

Paid US holidays

Performance raises — we reward people who grow

Long-term stability with a company that keeps its people



HOW TO APPLY — READ CAREFULLY

s that there is an unpaid $2,000 water bill on the property that must be resolved before closing. Your manager is in meetings all day. What do you do?

 is fine) introducing yourself and telling us why you're a fit for this role. Include the link in your application.

This is NOT a passive role. This is a high-output, daily-execution position. If you are looking for something to do a few hours a week, please do not apply.



DAILY RESPONSIBILITIES

Client Messaging (Every Day), Eastern US time hours (6AM EST - 3PM EST)



Reply to all client messages in Trainerize within the same business day, no exceptions

Send proactive check-in messages to clients who have not logged their workouts or meals

Provide accountability, encouragement, and coaching feedback on client logs

Escalate complex questions to the head coach with a clear summary of the situation

Flag any client who has gone silent for 48 or more hours

Maintain a professional, warm, and motivating tone in all messages



Meal Plan Updates (Every Day)



Review client food logs daily and make calorie or macro adjustments as directed

Update meal plan templates based on client preferences, allergies, and schedule changes

Ensure every active client has a current, up-to-date meal plan at all times

Flag clients who are consistently under- or over-eating and summarize for the head coach

Document all plan changes with a brief note for full head coach visibility



Workout Program Updates (Every Day)



Update client workout programs daily based on progress, injuries, equipment, or head coach direction

Swap exercises, adjust sets, reps, and load based on client feedback and logged performance

Keep programming at least one full week ahead for every active client at all times

Follow the specific exercise formatting and naming conventions used in PEAK Physique programs

Flag clients who are consistently skipping sessions or showing signs of overtraining



Progress Tracking



Log and organize weekly check-in data including weight, measurements, and progress photos

Prepare weekly progress summaries for the head coach

Monitor adherence metrics and alert the head coach to any at-risk clients

Maintain accurate, organized client notes inside Trainerize



Admin and Onboarding Support



Onboard new clients into Trainerize following the PEAK Physique checklist

Ensure client profiles, goals, and program assignments are correct from day one

Attend a weekly video call with the head coach for updates and priorities

Complete additional tasks assigned by the head coach within the agreed scope





WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR



Prior experience with Trainerize or a similar coaching platform (required)

Background in fitness, nutrition, or personal training (strong preference)

Excellent written English communication skills

Ability to work independently and meet daily deadlines without being followed up on

High attention to detail. One missed message or incorrect macro update can cost us a client

Reliable internet connection with consistent availability during your working hours

Coachable. You will receive direct, honest feedback and you are expected to implement it quickly

title: Automotive Service Advisor with Parts Estimating Experience for US company
description:
We are a busy independent auto repair shop in Louisiana, specializing in gas and diesel light/medium-duty vehicles. We do not do paint or collision work. We are seeking a remote service Advisor/Automotive Repair Order & Parts Estimating Specialist to join our team.



This is not a general virtual assistant position. We need someone with real automotive repair shop estimating experience who understands how to build complete, accurate repair orders inside Tekmetric for advisor review.



We work Monday-Friday, 8:00 AM-5:00 PM CST. This position requires someone willing to work our business hours, which will likely be a PHP graveyard shift. During scheduled work hours, you must be exclusively available to our shop.



Prior automotive repair shop estimating experience is required. Diesel and light/medium-duty vehicle experience is strongly preferred.



Duties:

* Build full draft repair orders inside Tekmetric for service advisor review

* Research and add all required parts for recommended repairs

* Review repair procedures using ALLDATA, Identifix, OEM information, MOTOR, and Tekmetric canned jobs

* Identify one-time-use and non-reusable parts such as torque-to-yield bolts, seals, gaskets, clips, hardware, and other required replacement items

* Add commonly missed parts such as O-rings, fluids, filters, clamps, shop supplies, seals, gaskets, and related components

* Research parts using OEC RepairLink, PartsTech, ATD, TireHub, TireCo, and vendor catalogs

* Communicate with vendors by message or phone when needed to get answers quickly

* Ask technicians for clarification when repair recommendations are unclear

* Build complete, profitable, sellable tickets that help advisors present the job confidently

* Check availability, pricing, fitment, part numbers, and delivery options

* Compare OEM, aftermarket, and tire options when appropriate

* Help prevent missed parts, wrong parts, underpriced tickets, and profit leaks

* Document notes clearly inside Tekmetric

* Follow internal estimating procedures and shop standards

* Assist with back-office estimating and parts-related tasks as needed



Experience Required:



* Prior automotive repair shop estimating experience

* Experience building repair orders or estimates for service advisors

* Strong understanding of gas and diesel light/medium-duty vehicles

* Ability to read repair procedures and identify required supporting parts

* Familiarity with fluids, seals, gaskets, hardware, torque-to-yield bolts, and non-reusable components

* Ability to spot parts that are commonly forgotten but required to complete the job correctly

* Experience with Tekmetric preferred

* Experience with OEC RepairLink, PartsTech, ATD, TireHub, TireCo, ALLDATA, Identifix, OEM repair information, and MOTOR preferred

* Strong English reading and writing skills required

* Clear spoken English preferred for vendor calls and team communication



Hiring Process & Must Haves:

* Will require video interviews

* Must be fluent in English reading and writing

* Must be able to communicate clearly with our team during work hours

* Must have prior automotive repair shop estimating experience

* Must be comfortable working Monday-Friday, 8:00 AM-5:00 PM CST

* Must have a Windows computer with current Windows OS

* Must have at least 16GB RAM

* Must have 2 monitors

* Must have reliable high-speed internet with backup connection

* Must have a noise-cancelling headset

* Must have a quiet workspace

* Must have voice chat ability for interviews and during work hours

* Must have a Payoneer account

* Must be willing to complete an estimating skills test

* Mandatory use of Timeproof



To Apply:



When applying, please use the
 subject:



“I know how to build complete repair orders with correct parts”



Please include:



* Your resume

* Your MS Teams ID

* A link to your OnlineJobs.ph profile

* Links to reviews from previous employers, if available

* A short explanation of your automotive estimating experience



Please answer the questions below:



1. How many years of automotive repair shop estimating experience do you have?

2. Have you built repair orders or estimates inside Tekmetric before?

3. Which systems have you used?

* Tekmetric

* OEC RepairLink

* PartsTech

* ATD

* TireHub

* TireCo

* ALLDATA

* Identifix

* OEM repair information

* MOTOR



4. Are you experienced with gas vehicles, diesel vehicles, or both?

5. Can you read a repair procedure and identify one-time-use parts, non-reusable parts, seals, gaskets, fluids, hardware, and other items needed to complete the job?

6. Give an example of a part or supply that is commonly forgotten on a repair estimate but can hurt profit if missed.

7. Are you comfortable calling or messaging vendors to confirm pricing, availability, fitment, and delivery time?

8. Are you okay working Monday-Friday, 8:00 AM-5:00 PM CST, which may be overnight where you are?

9. Do you have a Windows computer with at least 16GB RAM?



This role is for someone who understands that a good estimate is not just “find the main part and move on.” We need someone who can think like a parts manager, support the service advisors, protect technician productivity, and help us build complete tickets the first time.

title: Item Setup & Catalog Specialist
description:
Company Overview

We are a Los Angeles-based wholesale fine jewelry company established in 1972, supplying gold and silver jewelry to major national retailers, warehouse clubs, military exchanges, and leading e-commerce marketplaces. The company is building a lean, systems-driven operations team where accurate product data is treated as a competitive advantage.

 

Position Summary

We are looking for an experienced Item Setup & Catalog Specialist to own the complete lifecycle of product master data and retailer item onboarding.

This role is responsible for creating accurate product records in Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central, coordinating cross-functional teams to gather product assets, managing retailer portal uploads, maintaining retailer requirements documentation, and ensuring product data remains accurate throughout its lifecycle.

The ideal candidate is highly organized, detail-oriented, process-driven, and capable of managing multiple product launches while maintaining exceptional data accuracy.

 

Key Responsibilities

Product Master Data Management

• Create and maintain new product records in Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central.

• Ensure every item contains complete and accurate information before retailer submission, including:

o Vendor cost

o Cost of goods

o Metal type and fineness

o Product weight

o Dimensions

o UPC/GTIN

o Product hierarchy

• Maintain the ERP as the company's single source of truth.

Retailer Requirements Management

• Build and maintain a centralized retailer requirements matrix documenting:

o Image specifications

o Product description requirements

o Required attributes

o Pricing fields

o Compliance requirements

• Keep documentation current as retailer standards evolve.

Product Launch Coordination

• Coordinate with Sales, Merchandising, Warehouse, and Photography teams to collect all required launch assets.

• Identify missing information and proactively follow up until every requirement is completed.

• Track all outstanding launch requests through completion.

Retailer Portal Management

• Upload products into retailer and marketplace portals.

• Verify listings after publication.

• Resolve listing errors within 48 hours of discovery.

Product Data Governance

• Manage updates to:

o Product costs

o Pricing

o Metal cost adjustments

o Product discontinuations

• Maintain proper change logs and ensure Business Central remains accurate.

Competitive & Retailer Research

• Perform scheduled retailer and competitor assortment scrapes using company templates.

• Deliver structured pricing and assortment reports to Sales and Merchandising teams.

Documentation & SOP Development

• Create and maintain SOPs for:

o Item creation

o Retailer upload processes

o Product data management

o Retailer scraping procedures

• Continuously improve documentation for scalability and operational consistency.

 

Escalation Process

Tier 1

• Resolve missing information and routine retailer portal issues independently.

Tier 2

• Escalate ERP or Business Central technical issues to ERP support.

Tier 3

• Escalate any issue impacting committed retailer launch dates directly to the President.

 

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

• Less than 1% post-launch item setup error rate.

• 100% completion of Business Central item records before retailer uploads.

• Retailer requirements matrix reviewed and updated monthly.

• Product launches completed within retailer SLA once assets are received.

• 100% on-time delivery of scheduled retailer and competitor scrapes.

• Listing errors corrected within 48 hours.

 

Required Qualifications

• Minimum 2 years of experience in:

o Item setup

o Catalog management

o Product data operations

o Retail or e-commerce environments

• Experience onboarding products through retailer or marketplace portals such as:

o Walmart

o Sam's Club

o Amazon

o DSCO

o Similar enterprise retail platforms

• Experience working with ERP systems and item master data.

• Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central experience is highly preferred.

• Strong Microsoft Excel skills with experience handling structured datasets.

• Excellent written English communication skills.

• Strong organizational and follow-up abilities.

• Available to work with meaningful overlap during US Pacific business hours.

 

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience within jewelry, precious metals, or luxury products.

• Knowledge of:

o Gold karats

o Metal fineness

o Stone specifications

• Experience creating SOPs and operational documentation.

• Understanding of retailer image specifications, including resolution, aspect ratio, and background standards.

 

Ideal Candidate

The successful candidate will:

• Be exceptionally detail-oriented and process-driven.

• Take full ownership of product data quality.

• Be proactive in coordinating multiple stakeholders.

• Thrive in a fast-paced operational environment.

• Have strong ERP and catalog management experience.

• Consistently ensure products are retailer-ready with minimal errors.

• Take initiative in preventing issues rather than reacting to them.



How to apply:

Respond to this job post with your current resume, a short introduction video, your expected hourly rate, and why you're the best fit for this role.



Application should send all the needed requirements to be considered for this role.

description:
Read this first: We are only hiring senior AI video editors. If you are junior, still learning the tools, or looking for a place to grow into the role, this is not the position for you. We need someone who is already operating at a high level and can deliver from day one.



About us

We are a fast-growing DTC e-commerce brand in the wellness space. We run high volumes of paid video creative across Meta, and YouTube. Our creative is the engine of our growth, and we are scaling the volume and quality of what we produce using AI video tools. We need a senior editor who can lead that production.



What you will do

You will own the editing and assembly of our paid social video ads from start to finish. You will take scripts, raw UGC, AI-generated footage, and b-roll and turn them into scroll-stopping ads built to convert. You will use AI video and image tools to generate, extend, and enhance footage where needed. You will produce fast, iterate faster, and manage a high output of creative variations for testing without letting quality slip.



What we need from you

You are a senior editor. You have years of experience editing short-form paid video for DTC or performance brands, and you can show us the work. You are fluent in AI video generation and editing tools such as Runway, Kling, Higgsfield, Sora, Pika, ElevenLabs, and similar. You understand direct response, not just aesthetics. You know what makes someone stop scrolling and what makes an ad convert. You work fast without babysitting. You can take a script and a rough brief and deliver a finished ad without hand-holding.



You are a fit if

You have edited paid video that has actually run and driven results. You already use AI tools in your daily workflow, not as an experiment. You think in hooks, retention, and testing variations. You thrive on volume and speed. You have strong opinions about pacing, captions, sound design, and what makes creative perform.



You are not a fit if

You are early in your career. You need detailed direction on every project. You see AI tools as something you would like to learn rather than something you already use. You prioritize artistic polish over conversion performance.





How to apply

Send us your portfolio or reel of paid video work, a short note on which AI tools you use and how you use them in your workflow, and one example of an ad you edited that performed well and why you think it worked.

Want me to tailor the tone more aggressive or more polished, add specifics like salary range and location, or tighten it further? I can also write a shorter version for platforms like LinkedIn or a job board with character limits.

title: Jr. Remote Desktop Technician
description:
Location: Remote | Full-Time (US Business Hours, CST)

Company: Lockbaud



- About the Role -



Lockbaud is seeking a Jr. Remote Desktop Technician to provide technical support to a coast-to-coast U.S.-based user base. You’ll work tickets, take inbound calls, and learn by doing alongside experienced technicians.



We hire for three things in this role. Everything else is secondary.



1. Spark. Energy, personality, and a self-starting attitude. You take initiative without being chased.

2. You love technology for the sake of technology. Not just “I use a computer for work.” You tinker, build, break things on purpose, run a home lab, or stay up late figuring out why something failed. Curiosity is the point.

3. Real customer service experience. You’ve helped people under pressure before (retail, hospitality, call center, front desk, tech support, or similar). Users need someone patient, clear, and human on the phone.



You do not need years of MSP experience. You do need those three. Technical depth can be taught. Spark, genuine love of tech, and solid customer service instincts are much harder to fake.



- Key Responsibilities -



- Provide remote technical support to U.S.-based end users via ticketing system and inbound phone calls

- Communicate clearly and professionally with users, setting expectations and explaining issues in plain language

- Troubleshoot common Windows workstation and peripheral issues with guidance as needed

- Support basic Microsoft 365 issues (Outlook, Teams, OneDrive, password resets, and simple account tasks)

- Install and configure printer drivers, common software applications, and system updates

- Assist with basic VoIP phone troubleshooting under senior guidance

- Use remote access and RMM tools to diagnose and remediate endpoint issues

- Document troubleshooting steps, findings, and resolutions accurately in the ticketing system

- Escalate complex issues to senior technicians with clear context and supporting details

- Collaborate with the Lead Technician and Dispatch to keep ticket flow efficient

- Take ownership of learning: ask good questions, dig into unfamiliar issues, and build skill on the job



- Required Skills & Traits -



These are the non-negotiables:



- Spark: self-starter energy, personality, and initiative without constant direction

- Genuine love of technology for its own sake (home lab, personal projects, tinkering, or self-taught technical work)

- Prior customer service experience in a people-facing role (retail, hospitality, call center, front desk, help desk, or similar)

- Excellent spoken and written English, with the ability to communicate confidently over the phone

- Patient, clear, professional, and upbeat with live users

- Working knowledge of Windows operating systems (personal use counts if you can troubleshoot, not just click around)

- Willingness to learn and take ownership of unfamiliar technical issues

- Ability to remain calm and clear during live support interactions



- Preferred Qualifications -



- Home lab, homelab networking, or personal tech projects you can actually talk about

- Familiarity with Microsoft 365 (Outlook, Teams, OneDrive)

- Basic understanding of networking concepts (Wi-Fi, connectivity, simple DNS awareness)

- Prior phone-based or live chat support experience with U.S. customers

- Exposure to printers, peripherals, or basic VoIP devices

- CompTIA A+, Network+, or similar entry-level certs (nice to have, not required)

- Clear, neutral, or American-accented English (for phone-based support)



- What Success Looks Like -



- Users feel helped, not rushed or confused

- You bring energy and personality without sacrificing professionalism

- You dig into problems because you actually want to understand them

- You ask smart questions and document what you tried

- You own your tickets and follow through instead of waiting to be poked

- You improve week over week: fewer handoffs on simple issues, stronger technical judgment



- Growth Path -



This role is a strong entry point into Lockbaud’s support team. There isn’t a rigid promotion ladder with fixed checkpoints, but technicians who show ownership, technical growth, and strong customer communication naturally take on broader work and more complex tickets. If you want to grow into a full Remote Desktop Technician scope, the opportunity is here for people who earn it.



- Why Lockbaud -



You’ll support real users in real environments, not a scripted call center queue. You’ll get exposure to Microsoft platforms, printers, VoIP, and multi-client MSP work while building both technical and communication skills. We value grit, curiosity, and people who actually like this stuff.



- How to Apply -



- Include “ExcitedToStart!” at the beginning of your application

- Submit a resume that clearly shows customer service experience

- In a short note, tell us: (1) something technical you’ve fixed or built for fun, and (2) a customer service 
nt you’re proud of

- Include a short voice recording to demonstrate phone communication skills

title: Remote Desktop Technician
description:
Location: Remote | Full-Time (US Business Hours, CST)

Company: Lockbaud



- About the Role -



Lockbaud is seeking a Remote Desktop Technician to provide technical support to a coast-to-coast U.S.-based user base. This role involves frequent live interaction with end users and requires excellent spoken and written English, strong communication skills, and the ability to explain technical concepts clearly and confidently.



The technician will support primarily Microsoft-based environments and must be comfortable learning new systems and troubleshooting a wide variety of issues. One ticket may involve installing a printer driver. The next may require diagnosing a VoIP phone problem. Success in this role depends on curiosity, adaptability, and clear communication as much as technical ability.



- Key Responsibilities -



- Provide remote technical support to U.S.-based end users via ticketing system and inbound phone calls

- Communicate clearly and professionally with users, setting expectations and explaining technical issues in plain language

- Troubleshoot and resolve issues on Windows workstations and peripherals

- Support Microsoft 365 applications, including Outlook, Teams, OneDrive, and user account-related issues

- Install and configure printer drivers, software applications, and system updates

- Assist with troubleshooting VoIP phone systems, including device configuration, connectivity, and basic call quality issues

- Use remote access and RMM tools to diagnose and remediate endpoint issues

- Document troubleshooting steps, findings, and resolutions accurately in the ticketing system

- Escalate complex issues with clear context and supporting details

- Collaborate with Lead Technician and Dispatch to maintain efficient ticket flow



- Required Skills & Traits -



- Excellent spoken and written English, with the ability to communicate confidently over the phone

- Strong customer-facing communication skills; ability to work directly with a U.S.-based user population

- Willingness to learn and take ownership of unfamiliar technical issues

- Experience in a technical support or service desk role, or equivalent hands-on technical experience

- Working knowledge of Windows operating systems

- Ability to remain calm, clear, and professional (and upbeat) during live support interactions



- Preferred Qualifications -



- Familiarity with Microsoft 365 environments

- Basic understanding of networking concepts (connectivity, DNS awareness, VoIP fundamentals)

- Prior experience providing phone-based technical support to U.S. customers

- Familiarity with VoIP phone systems and endpoint hardware

- Experience supporting printers and peripheral devices

- MSP or multi-client support experience

- Clear, neutral, or American-accented English (for phone-based support roles)



- What Success Looks Like -



- Users understand what you’re doing and why

- Issues are resolved efficiently without unnecessary escalation

- Documentation is thorough and useful to other technicians

- You handle unfamiliar problems methodically instead of freezing



- Why Lockbaud -



This role offers hands-on experience supporting real users in real environments. You’ll work directly with U.S.-based customers, gain exposure to Microsoft platforms, printers, and VoIP systems, and develop your technical and communication skills alongside experienced technicians.



- How to Apply -



- Include “ExcitedToStart!” at the beginning of your application

- Submit a resume highlighting technical experience and customer-facing work

- Include a short voice recording to demonstrate phone communication skills

title: Social Media Content Editor (Instagram Reels/TikTok)
description:
Schedule: Monday-Friday availability preferred

Remote Position



We are hiring a highly creative, detail-oriented, and coachable Short-Form Video Editor & Social Media Assistant to join our growing real estate media company serving the DMV area.



This is not just an editing role. We are looking for someone who genuinely understands modern short-form content and wants to help grow visibility, engagement, relationships, and overall business opportunities through social media.



You will help create engaging reels and short-form content for real estate agents, listings, behind-the-scenes media, and agent-focused branding across Instagram Reels, TikTok,
 Reels, and YouTube Shorts.



This role starts focused primarily on content creation and editing, but there is strong long-term growth potential for the right person to eventually take on broader social media management responsibilities as the company continues to grow.



If you naturally pay attention to social media trends, understand what makes people stop scrolling, and enjoy helping brands grow online, this may be a great fit for you.



What You’ll Do

• Edit short-form vertical video content optimized for Instagram Reels, TikTok,
 Reels, and YouTube Shorts

• Create engaging, retention-focused edits using strong hooks, pacing, captions, trending audio, and modern editing styles

• Assist with content posting and optimization across multiple platforms

• Maintain organization and consistency across content workflows

• Double-check captions, formatting, audio, exports, thumbnails, and post quality before publishing

• Track engagement trends and key performance metrics over time

• Monitor retention, reach, saves, shares, comments, and overall content performance

• Help identify which content styles and topics are performing best

• Assist with collaboration ideas involving agents, affiliates, and local businesses

• Bring proactive content and growth suggestions to the table instead of simply posting passively

• Help increase overall brand visibility through stronger video distribution and social engagement strategies



Compensation & Growth Path

• Starting pay: $4-$6/hour depending on experience and skill level

• Part-time role to start (approximately 10-12 hours per week)

• Opportunity for increased hours and compensation as responsibilities grow

• Long-term potential to expand into broader social media management and content strategy responsibilities

• Opportunity to grow with a fast-moving real estate media company focused heavily on video and brand expansion



What We’re Looking For

• Strong CapCut editing experience highly preferred

• Strong understanding of short-form content pacing, hooks, captions, and retention-focused editing

• Actively understands and consumes Instagram Reels, TikTok, and modern social content trends

• Extremely detail-oriented and organized

• Reliable and consistent with deadlines

• Strong communication skills

• Positive attitude and coachable mindset

• Creative thinker who takes initiative

• Comfortable receiving feedback and implementing revisions quickly

• Ability to work independently while staying communicative

• Canva experience is a plus for simple graphics and carousels

This Role May NOT Be For You If:

• You dislike fast-moving environments

• You struggle with consistency or meeting deadlines

• You prefer minimal communication or collaboration

• You only want to “edit videos” without thinking strategically about engagement and growth

• You dislike feedback or revisions

• You tend to rush through details like captions, formatting, or audio quality



Why This Role Is Great

• Flexible remote schedule

• Clear long-term growth potential

• Opportunity to help shape a growing media brand

• Creative and collaborative work environment

• Chance to build valuable social media strategy experience

• Opportunity to work closely with real estate professionals and growing businesses

• Consistent opportunity to improve editing, branding, and content strategy skills



Application Instructions

When applying, please include:

title: Curriculum Developer
description:
Contract Curriculum and Educational Product Developer



Position Overview



Seeking a creative and experienced Contract Curriculum and Educational Product Developer to create a market-ready curriculum and a collection of printable educational cards based on a current program.



The contractor will work closely with program leadership to transform the organization’s existing programming, activities, recipes, and social-emotional learning concepts into professional products that can be purchased and used by schools, community organizations, families, educators, counselors, and the general public.



This is a project-based contract position. The curriculum and card products will be developed together as one coordinated educational product line.



The program e is a youth-focused program that uses cooking, teamwork, conversation, and guided reflection to strengthen belonging, confidence, communication, resilience, and help-seeking skills.



The program combines hands-on culinary activities with meaningful lessons that help participants develop practical life skills and stronger connections with others.



Project Responsibilities



The contractor will be responsible for:



Reviewing existing curriculum, recipes, activities, program materials, outcomes, and educational goals.

Organizing the program into a clear, structured, and easy-to-use curriculum.

Creating separate versions or adaptations suitable for schools and the general public.

Developing lesson plans that include learning objectives, required materials, preparation instructions, activities, discussion questions, reflection prompts, and facilitator guidance.

Creating participant worksheets, activity pages, journal prompts, and supporting educational materials.

Developing a collection of printable cards that reinforce lessons and can be sold as a standalone product or used alongside the curriculum.

Creating card concepts such as conversation cards, reflection cards, teamwork challenges, coping-skill prompts, cooking challenges, encouragement cards, and family discussion cards.

Writing clear, engaging, age-appropriate, and emotionally sensitive card content.

Organizing the cards into categories, themes, or sets that are easy for customers to understand and use.

Creating instructions explaining how educators, families, facilitators, and community organizations can use the cards.

Working with Kitchen of Life leadership to ensure the products reflect the organization’s mission, language, values, and teaching approach.

Revising the curriculum and cards based on feedback.

Preparing final materials for professional design, printing, digital sale, or distribution.

Helping identify appropriate product formats, packaging ideas, card quantities, curriculum sections, and potential bundles.

Curriculum Deliverables



The final curriculum may include:



Curriculum overview and program introduction

Facilitator or teacher guide

Recommended age groups and settings

Learning objectives

Complete lesson plans

Cooking activities and recipes

Social-emotional learning activities

Discussion and reflection questions

Participant worksheets

Supply and ingredient lists

Classroom and group-management guidance

School implementation instructions

General-public or family-use instructions

Assessment, feedback, or reflection tools

Suggestions for adapting activities for different ages and group sizes

Recommendations for curriculum packaging and sale

Educational Card Deliverables



The contractor will create a coordinated collection of  cards that may include:



Belonging and connection cards

Communication cards

Teamwork cards

Confidence and competency cards

Choice and autonomy cards

Community-building cards

Reflection and conversation cards

Cooking challenge cards

Family discussion cards

Encouragement or affirmation cards

Facilitator instruction cards



Final card content should be organized into clearly defined sets and prepared in a format that can be provided to a graphic designer or printer.



Ideal Qualifications



The ideal contractor will have experience in one or more of the following areas:



Curriculum development

Educational product development

Social-emotional learning

Youth programming

Classroom teaching

School-based programming

Instructional design

Educational card or game development

Nonprofit program development

Writing for children, teenagers, families, or educators

Culinary education or experiential learning



The contractor should also demonstrate:



Strong writing, editing, and organizational skills

The ability to turn existing program ideas into structured, marketable products

Experience writing clear instructions for educators and facilitators

Creativity in developing engaging activities and card prompts

An understanding of age-appropriate and trauma-informed language

Attention to detail and consistency

The ability to receive feedback and complete revisions

Strong communication and project-management skills

The ability to meet agreed-upon deadlines



Experience working with mental-health education, suicide-prevention organizations, schools, or youth-serving nonprofits is preferred but not required.



Project Structure



This is a contract-based project with specific milestones, deliverables, and deadlines established before the project begins.



The selected contractor will work collaboratively with Kitchen of Life leadership and may participate in scheduled meetings to review concepts, drafts, revisions, and final materials.



Applicants should provide:



All final curriculum materials, card content, worksheets, lesson plans, product concepts, and related materials created under this contract will become the exclusive property of Kitchen of Life upon full payment, unless otherwise agreed to in writing.



The contractor may not sell, reproduce, distribute, publish, or reuse proprietary materials without written permission.



The contractor will be expected to maintain the confidentiality of the programs internal materials, participant information, program strategies, and unpublished content.

title: Senior Web Developer
description:
Job Description





The Ad Firm is a Digital Marketing Agency based in Southern California, serving clients nationwide. Since 2009, we’ve helped businesses grow through SEO, content, and performance-driven digital strategies.



We’re expanding our team and looking for a Senior Web Developer to lead how our websites are built from the ground up. This is not a production role. This is a systems-level engineering role for someone who understands that websites are not just design deliverables, they are performance assets that need to rank, scale, and hold up under real-world conditions.



This is a remote position with flexible working hours from day one.





About the Role



Own the technical foundation of the websites we build

Architect, develop, and optimize custom builds for SEO, performance, and scalability

Work closely with SEO, Content, and Digital PR teams to ensure strong technical execution

Build systems that are clean, scalable, and maintainable

Focus on engineering quality over page builders or pre-built themes



Key Responsibilities



Architect and build fully custom WordPress websites (themes, plugins, ACF-driven structures)

Engineer sites for speed, scalability, and strong Core Web Vitals performance

Handle server environments, deployments, and infrastructure decisions

Integrate APIs and third-party systems cleanly and reliably

Own technical SEO implementation (crawlability, indexation, structured data)

Manage DNS, CDN (Cloudflare), SMTP, and hosting configurations

Work across Shopify and BigCommerce at the code level when needed

Implement accurate tracking (GA4, GTM) without compromising data integrity

Debug issues across the full stack (server, backend, frontend performance)



What We’re Looking For



5+ years of web development experience in agency or performance-driven environments

Deep expertise in PHP (including WordPress core-level development)

Strong JavaScript experience with modern frameworks and tooling

Working knowledge of Python (automation, scraping, tooling)

Proven experience building custom WordPress websites from scratch

Strong understanding of technical SEO and its impact on architecture and performance

Ability to diagnose and solve full-stack issues independently



What Sets You Apart



You think in systems, not pages

Experience working on large-scale or SEO-heavy websites

Strong understanding of crawlability, indexation, and internal linking at scale

Experience with schema and structured data implementation

Exposure to programmatic SEO or dynamic page generation

Experience handling real-world constraints (traffic spikes, broken deployments, legacy rebuilds)



Strong Advantages



Experience with CI/CD pipelines and Git workflows

Familiarity with Docker or modern dev environments

Experience with log analysis and advanced debugging

Security hardening and site recovery experience

Experience with multi-site or multi-location SEO builds



What We Don’t Want



Heavy reliance on page builders

Plugin-first approaches to performance and SEO

Developers who need constant direction or step-by-step instructions



Why Join Us?



High ownership with real technical decision-making

Clean builds with no unnecessary bloat

Direct collaboration with SEO, Content, and Digital PR specialists

A team that values performance, scalability, and engineering quality

Competitive salary and performance-based incentives

Flexible remote work from day one

2 weeks Paid Time-Off

Paid Sick Leave

8 Paid Holidays

Health Insurance



Ready to Apply?



Submit your resume

Include a portfolio with examples of custom builds

Add a short note on how you approach building high-performance websites



How to Apply:

s on this website. Submit your application at

title: Remote Leasing Assistant
description:
About Us

Los Angeles property management company managing a large residential portfolio. Our leasing team turns rental applications into clean, owner-ready approval packages. Accuracy and consistency matter enormously — owners make decisions off our write-ups, and a single wrong number or missing verification creates real problems.



The Role

You will process rental applications from start to finish and produce owner-ready “vetted app” packages, following our detailed written SOP exactly. This is precise, checklist-driven work with real judgment: verifying income, reading financial documents, making verification calls, and composing structured summaries that go to property owners for approval.



What You'll Do

? Assemble complete application packages — confirm every adult applicant's ID, application, credit, and background check are present.

? Verify income against our 2.5×-rent threshold, converting pay frequencies correctly and applying our rules for overtime, gig, self-employed, and voucher income.

? Review 3 months of bank statements and the credit report; flag red flags (negative balances, sharp declines, derogatory items) accurately.

? Verify employment and rental history by phone with employers and landlords, and document the results in our standard language.

? Handle Section 8 / Housing Choice Voucher applications — capture voucher details, check bedroom-size match and expiration, and run the alternative income test.

? Compose the vetted-app
 in our exact format and subject-line convention, with correct routing — and catch the common errors before they go out.

? Monitor owner responses and prepare the congratulations letter and internal lease-for-approval once approved.

? Assemble the lease from the approved application and property record, then prepare and send the DocuSign envelope to the correct signer (which varies by property type).

? Monitor the leasing inbox throughout the day — owner approvals, outside-agent messages, and applicant replies — and move each file to its next step promptly.

What We're Looking For

? Exceptional attention to detail. This role lives or dies on accuracy — correct numbers, complete fields, no typos in addresses or figures.

? Strong written English (owner- and applicant-facing
s must be clean and professional) and clear spoken English (you'll call U.S. employers and landlords to verify).

? Comfort with numbers — percentages, pay-frequency conversions, and threshold math done reliably by hand.

? Ability to follow a long, detailed SOP precisely and apply judgment on edge cases rather than guessing.

? Discretion with sensitive financial and personal information.

? Reliable computer, stable internet (?25 Mbps) with a backup connection, and a backup-power plan.

? A plus: experience in property management, leasing, mortgage/loan underwriting, insurance, or BPO back-office work; AppFolio; or familiarity with U.S. Section 8 / HACLA.



How to Apply — Read Carefully

To be considered, your application MUST include all of the following. Applications missing any item will not be reviewed.

1 Internet speed proof. A Speedtest.net screenshot showing at least 25 Mbps download.

2 A quick math check (show your work): The rent is $2,095/month. An applicant's only income is a bi-weekly paycheck with gross pay of $3,391.83. (a) What is the minimum monthly income we require? (b) What is the applicant's monthly income? (c) Do they qualify?

3 A short writing sample. Write a brief, professional
 to an applicant telling them their bank statements were incomplete — you need the 3 most recent statements from one account, as PDFs (not screenshots).

4 Three short answers (a few sentences each): (a) Describe any experience you have reviewing financial documents, verifying information, or processing applications. (b) How do you make sure you don't miss details in repetitive work? (c) Your current internet provider and your backup plan for outages.

5 Your rate. Expected hourly rate in USD and earliest availability.

Why these? The math and writing questions mirror the actual daily work. Strong applications that follow instructions move to a short paid skills test, a video call, and reference checks.



Our Process

? Application review against the requirements above.

? Short paid skills test (process a sample rental application into a vetted-app write-up).

? Video interview.

? Reference checks, then offer.

title: Government Contracts & Proposal Coordinator
description:
1.1 Mission

The Coordinator's mission: never miss a deadline, never submit an incomplete proposal, never lose a contract to paperwork, and maintain 100% compliance — while building a repeatable bidding machine that scales with the company.

The Coordinator is the air-traffic controller of every pursuit. Estimators price the work; project teams build it; leadership sets strategy. The Coordinator makes sure that every opportunity is found, qualified, assembled, compliance-checked, and submitted on time, complete, and correct — every single time.



1.2 Purpose of the Role

Government work is won or lost on discipline. A brilliant price on an incomplete package loses. A perfect technical proposal submitted one minute late loses. A missing certification voids an award. The Coordinator exists to remove those failure modes permanently by operating the systems in this manual.

. Find and track every relevant opportunity across all portals.

. Qualify opportunities with a disciplined Go/No-Go process before we spend estimating hours.

. Assemble complete, compliant bid packages using standardized checklists.

. Coordinate estimators, subcontractors, and suppliers so information arrives on time.

. Run quality assurance so no proposal leaves the building with an error.

. Submit flawlessly, capture confirmations, and archive everything.

. Manage post-award compliance setup so we start projects clean.

. Maintain the document library, databases, and compliance calendar as living systems.



Daily, Weekly, Monthly & Annual Responsibilities



The role runs on rhythm. These checklists convert the mission into repeatable habits.



2.1 Morning Checklist (first 90 minutes)

.  Review the Deadline Tracker; confirm every open bid's due date, time, and time zone.

.  Check all portal notifications (
, NJSTART, BidNet Direct, PennBid, county/municipal, school, housing authority) for new opportunities and, critically, new addenda/amendments.

.  Log any new addenda in the Addenda Log for every active pursuit and flag scope/price impacts to the estimator.

.  Scan
 for subcontractor/supplier quotes, RFI responses, and agency communications; file and log each.

.  Update the Opportunity Tracker status for anything that changed overnight.

.  Identify today's single most important deadline and block time to protect it.

.  Raise any red flags (missing bond, expiring insurance, unclear spec) to your manager before 10:00 a.m.



2.2 Afternoon Checklist



.  Advance the top-priority bid package: assemble documents, request missing items, update the checklist.

.  Follow up on outstanding subcontractor/supplier quotes and RFIs with a written, logged request.

.  Verify that any addenda received today are incorporated into the estimate and the package.

.  Confirm bonding and insurance are in motion for bids due within 7 days.

.  Update the Question Log; submit any pre-bid questions well before the solicitation's question deadline.

.  Perform a mid-stage QA pass on any package reaching 75% completion.



2.3 End-of-Day Checklist



.  Reconcile the Deadline Tracker: every active bid has an accurate status and next action.

.  Confirm nothing due tomorrow is incomplete; if it is, escalate tonight — not tomorrow.

.  Save and version all working files; sync SharePoint/OneDrive.

.  Write a two-line end-of-day status for your manager: what advanced, what is blocked.

.  Set tomorrow's top three priorities.



2.4 Weekly Responsibilities



.  Run saved searches across all portals and refresh the pipeline; add new qualified opportunities.

.  Hold a bid-review huddle with estimating: priorities, due dates, resource conflicts.

.  Audit the document library for anything expiring in the next 45 days.

.  Update the KPI dashboard (opportunities reviewed, packages in progress, submissions).

.  Reconcile subcontractor/supplier database additions and note coverage gaps by trade and region.

.  Back up all active bid folders and confirm version control is clean.



2.5 Monthly Responsibilities



.  Full document-library expiration audit (insurance, bonds capacity, registrations, licenses, certifications).

.  Pipeline review with leadership: win rate, hit rate, revenue-weighted pipeline, capacity.

.  Post-bid debrief roll-up: wins, losses, pricing gaps, lessons learned.

. Verify 
 registration status and renewal timeline; confirm UEI/CAGE active.

.  Refresh saved searches and NAICS coverage; prune dead portals, add new ones.

.  Update templates and this manual with any process improvements approved during the month.



2.6 Quarterly Responsibilities



.  Comprehensive compliance self-audit.

.  Bonding capacity review with the surety/broker; update aggregate and single-job limits.

.  Insurance program review with the broker; confirm limits meet target agencies' requirements.

.  Subcontractor prequalification refresh cycle; re-collect expiring COIs and certifications.

.  KPI trend review and goal reset for the next quarter.

.  Portal registration renewals check (state/county/municipal vendor registrations).



2.7 Annual Responsibilities

 annual renewal (do not let it lapse — an expired registration blocks federal awards).

title: Paid Media & Lead Generation Specialist — Meta, Google, Landing Pages & CRM

WHAT YOU WILL OWN

, and Instagram lead-generation and conversion campaigns

Contractual | California business hours | Compensation is based on experience, depth of B2B SEO/content expertise, and demonstrated results. There is strong potential for compensation growth based on performance and impact within the first 3–6 months. 



THE AMBITION



CDMS is a 17-person environmental, health & safety consulting firm serving California industrial and commercial facilities since 1988. We intend to become the most trusted EHS compliance partner in California, and we're investing seriously to get there. Marketing is one of the main levers, alongside service quality and technical depth.



Two assets are already in motion: a large-scale content and search program across our core services on 
, and a second publication, EHS Career Paths (
), that reaches EHS professionals directly. Until now this work has been handled within the team, without a dedicated owner. This role is that owner.



THE ROLE



Marketing at CDMS is several disciplines running at once: SEO and content operations, local search and reputation, off-site authority building, and the design and conversion work that turns visits into leads. A firm our size can't hire a specialist for each. We need one person who runs it all as a system: doing the project management for the full portfolio of marketing work at CDMS, doing a lot of the core & high leverage work personally & via automations, and working with internal and external partners for the rest.



At CDMS (about two-thirds)



The content pipeline: keep service pages, cluster content, and blog posts moving from draft to published, with our web developer.

Local search and reputation: Google reviews, Business Profile, citations, local landing pages.

Conversion: page design, calls to action, and the authority signals that make a prospect pick up the phone and that make a client pick us for the work.

The weekly dashboard: traffic, rankings, leads. Tell us what the numbers mean, not just what they are.





At EHS Career Paths (about one-third, ramping up)



The publishing engine: articles, newsletter, practitioner interviews, and repurposing each piece across formats and channels.

Growth: outreach to associations and university programs, the LinkedIn presence, and the annual State of EHS in California survey.



Example projects in the first year



Build the local reputation engine: run the Google review program with our project managers and stand up local landing pages, so facilities searching in our service areas find us and trust what they see.

Redesign our highest-traffic service pages for conversion: layout, calls to action, and proof elements, measured in calls and quote requests rather than traffic.

Launch the first State of EHS in California survey: design it, distribute it through associations and university programs, and publish the report as the best California dataset in the field.



WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR



An architect, not an operator. Someone analytical and systems-minded who turns ambiguity into structure instead of waiting for instructions, and who measures themselves on outcomes rather than completed tasks. A power user of AI and modern tools who would rather automate a process than repeat it. Someone who enjoys the problem-solving itself, because we are in the process of figuring out the playbook. Excellent written English is required; the work is audience-facing in English.



THE PROCESS



Our hiring process flexes with each conversation, but the common elements are consistent: a short behavioral assessment, a 12-minute reasoning test, interviews, a review of past work, and reference checks with your former direct managers.



Next Step: To move forward in the hiring process, please complete the assessment below. Once finished, you’ll receive a second assessment. Completion of both is required for consideration.
